      Key inferences

        Areas to improve: recommended actions

          How to read these numbers

          • Coverage % = ZD covered ÷ ZD reported for the same UC and campaign. Target: 90% or above.
          • Like-for-like trend: April vs May uses only UCs that reported coverage in both campaigns, so the smaller May SNID doesn't distort the result.
          • Over 110% usually points to a data issue (children covered from other UCs, catch-up children, or ZDs under-reported), not strong performance.
          • Zero covered where ZDs were reported often means coverage wasn't recorded. Confirm before acting on it as a field failure.
          • ZDs per 1,000 households compares burden across areas of different size. A rise can mean better detection of zero-dose children.
          • Not analysed: two unlabelled columns in the Sept sheet (after "AFP Cases") were left out.

          District notes

          Ordered by rating, with the places that need attention first. Each note gives the coverage trend, the gap, the Sept caseload and the focus UCs.

          SNID Sept double-risk UCs: last coverage <80% and more ZDs reported now

          "Last coverage" = SNID May, or NID April for UCs not in May. These UCs had a coverage problem last time and a larger zero-dose caseload in Sept. Prioritise them when Sept coverage is collected.
          Data: ZERO DOSE VALIDATION DATA.xlsx · 18,103 children validated on 2,580 forms in 774 UCs, 37 districts · 7 campaigns (NID FEB 2026, NID APR 2026, SNID May 2026, KP-Special-1-Jul 2026, KP Special Aug 2026, KP Special Aug-Sep 2026-3, SNID Sep 2026) · entries 20-Jan-2026 to 06-Oct-2026. % vaccinated = children the validator confirmed as vaccinated ÷ children validated.

Over 100% usually means the target is set too low or children from other areas were vaccinated here. Dropout = share of children who got the first dose but not the later one.

          All UCs

          One row per EPI-MIS union council. "Polio UC" shows whether the UC was matched to the polio UC list (used for the comparison with zero-dose data). Click a column header to sort.
          UCs are flagged when Penta-3 is below 80%, more than 10% drop out between Penta-1 and Penta-3, more than 20% drop out between MR-1 and MR-2, any of Penta-1, Penta-3 or MR-1 is over 110% (check the target), or the UC has no target. Weak in EPI and polio means low routine coverage (Penta-1 below 90% or Penta-3 below 80%) and a polio warning sign in the same UC: zero-dose coverage below 80%, or many zero-dose children reported in Sept for its size. Dropouts are only flagged where at least 20 children got the first dose.

            What the risk score says

              UCs ranked by risk score

              Score = points earned ÷ points possible for the indicators each UC has data for. Surveillance covers every UC, so the zero-dose AFP (3) and polio case (5) points always count as possible. LQAS (4) counts only for UCs assessed in the last rounds, so a passed lot is evidence that lowers the score. "Data" = how many of the 4 main indicators (ZD coverage, digitized, validated, Penta-3) the UC has. Treat scores based on 1 indicator with care.

              What the watch list says

                District watch ranking

                District watch score = average of its 5 highest UC scores. The top 6 districts are the watch districts. "No sewage site" means the district has no environmental sampling, so virus could circulate without being seen.

                UCs ranked by polio risk

                This is a watch list for focusing supervision, catch-up campaigns, AFP active search and sewage sampling, not a prediction. With about 20 cases a year, most UCs on the list will not have a case, and a case can still appear outside it.

                What the critical review says

                  UCs where reported coverage and other checks disagree

                  Reported ZD coverage = covered ÷ reported zero-dose children in the latest campaign with coverage data. A UC is listed when it reports 90%+ coverage but an independent check disagrees (latest LQAS lot not passed, under 90% of validated children vaccinated, Penta-3 under 60%, or a zero-dose AFP case), or when more children were entered in IDIMS than were reported. These UCs need a field check before their numbers are used.

                      UCs with the most children still missed

                      Still missed = children recorded as missed (not available or refused) who were still not vaccinated after the campaign, catch-up and extended catch-up, plus "left over" children in areas the teams did not finish. Percentages are of the household target (children under 5). Persistent refusals = 20 or more children still refusing in every 2026 campaign the UC took part in.
